title: Bake-off (hos): deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017
question: Who holds power in NEAR’s House of Stake? Make me a fresh flower, not an existing one.
note: A real run on NEAR AI Cloud (T060), kept with the signature each completion got. A hash or link the model copied from a tool result is written as a reference to that result ($from, {{…}}), so it replays on recordedClient.

turns.content: I'll start by finding the network.

interpretation.summary: Power in NEAR's House of Stake is veNEAR voting power: NEAR locked in lockups, weighted by lock length, minus votes delegated out and plus votes delegated in. 519 participants hold 5,364,517 veNEAR in total. The top five accounts hold just over half of it, and the ten largest about 81%, so a small set of delegates and lockers decides most votes. Two of the five largest holders are implicit accounts with no name at all.

power_means.claim: Power is veNEAR voting power, the contract's rule: own locked veNEAR minus outgoing delegations plus incoming ones.
Five accounts together cross the 50% line: the Nakamoto coefficient at a 0.5 threshold is 5.
The ten largest hold 81.1% of voting power, while the 405 smallest together hold 0.014%.
Delegation is concentrated too: 145 accounts delegate to 42 delegates, and 3,340,900 veNEAR is delegated in total; five delegates hold 52.7% of that.

mappings.why: Square-root of each account's share of veNEAR voting power, so the largest bars lead but the long tail stays visible.
Share of voting power, compressed into a band of at most 2x, so every petal's bar has room.
Named account (self-declared account id) versus anonymous implicit account, so unnamed large holders stand out.
Solid where the name is only self-declared, none where the identity is unknown.
Most voting power first, clockwise from the top.

conflicts: Proposal-making and role-holding (the venear.dao and vote.dao configs) are separate kinds of influence, and this flower does not draw them.
Off-chain influence — forum standing, delegate profiles, social weight — is not measurable here and is not drawn.
unknowns: Who is behind an address: names are self-declared account ids, not verified people. Addresses are not people.
Whether the two largest holders (implicit accounts) are individuals, teams, or intermediaries.
Per-voter votes on the 30 proposals, and their lockup contracts and staking, are not read.
Delegation is measured at one final block; it changes as holders re-delegate.
inferred: That the largest accounts are delegates or institutional lockers rather than many individuals sharing control is an inference from the delegation figures, not a fact read from the chain.
Overlap between a delegate's own lock and its delegated-in power is not separated, so a single entity may appear in more than one large bar.
